real: Alright, clean up the schema and then move on
prev_agent: Yes—your instinct is right. We already had `tenants.domain`, which is persisted, unique, and trusted. The new `canonicalRootUrl` is technically a full URL, but its validator requires HTTPS, the exact same hostname, and no port/path/query/fragment. Therefore every valid value is necessarily `https://${domain}`. See [tenants.ts](/Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/06f8/evorto/src/db/schema/tenants.ts:34) and [tenant-origin.ts](/Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/06f8/evorto/src/shared/tenant-origin.ts:61). The vulnerability was not the absence of a root URL—it was constructing registration links from request headers. We can securely derive the origin from the persisted domain and remove `canonicalRootUrl` from the schema, forms, and contracts. I recommend doing that before merge; it also eliminates the required-column rollout/backfill problem. On serialization: I would not claim it is performance-proven. Static review shows low immediate risk: - There is no tenant-wide mutex. Registration/waitlist lock one membership row, so only concurrent actions by the same user in the same tenant serialize ([event-registration.service.ts](/Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/06f8/evorto/src/server/effect/rpc/handlers/events/event-registration.service.ts:1432)). - Stripe calls and actual email delivery are outside database transactions. Transactional email work is only an outbox insert. - Registration, payment, and membership lookups generally have suitable unique/partial indexes. - Same-option capacity updates remain a natural hot row, but that contention existed before this change. However, I found two conditional scaling gaps: 1. Cancellation locks all transactions for a registration, but there is no general index for `(tenantId, eventRegistrationId, type)` ([events-registration.handlers.ts](/Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/06f8/evorto/src/server/effect/rpc/handlers/events/events-registration.handlers.ts:317)). The pending-only index does not cover successful transactions. 2. The tenant active-registration-limit query filters by tenant and user, while the new index orders `(tenantId, eventId, userId)` ([event-registrations.ts](/Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/06f8/evorto/src/db/schema/event-registrations.ts:46)). Large tenants would benefit from a partial `(tenantId, userId, eventId)` active-registration index. There is also a small deadlock risk if overlapping add-ons are updated in different orders; sorting add-on IDs before updates would remove that. The PostgreSQL tests prove two-connection correctness and blocking, not throughput or p99 latency ([registration-concurrency.postgres.spec.ts](/Users/hedde/.codex/worktrees/06f8/evorto/src/db/schema/registration-concurrency.postgres.spec.ts:429)). My recommendation before merge is: remove redundant `canonicalRootUrl`, add the transaction index, consider the per-user active index, sort …
